ATHTR 500: This course provides a foundational overview of evidence-based practice (EBP) in the health sciences, which includes an overview of the seven steps of the EBP process.
ATHTR 501: This course provides an overview of various biobehavioral factors that underpin the enhancement of human capabilities, including, but not limited to, kinesthesia, physical fitness, and motor coordination in diverse physically active populations.
ATHTR 800: This course provides a dedicated overview of athletic training using the most current Board of Certification Practice Analysis and Standards of Professional Practice as a framework for learning.
ATHTR 801: This course provides an opportunity for students to become proficient in the knowledge and skills related to contemporary prehospital emergency medical care provided by athletic trainers.
ATHTR 802: This course uses a regional approach to study the gross anatomical structures of the human body.
ATHTR 803: This will be the first in a series of evaluation-based courses for the Master of Athletic Training degree program, and will cover key concepts of the evaluative process.
ATHTR 804: This course will focus on the etiology, evaluation and rehabilitation of injuries to the lower extremities typically encountered by physically active individuals.
ATHTR 805: This represents the initial opportunity for athletic training students to engage in the application of theory and foundational athletic training, knowledge, and skills through hands-on patient/client care experiences for 10-to-15 hours per week (150-to-225 total hours for the semester).
ATHTR 806: This course will focus on the etiology, evaluation and rehabilitation of injuries to the upper extremities typically encountered by physically active individuals.
ATHTR 807: This course will provide athletic training students will the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively function as a versatile primary care service provider.
ATHTR 808: This course provides the theoretical underpinnings that drive clinical applications of therapeutic interventions in health care and human performance restoration practice settings.
ATHTR 809: This reflects the second clinical education experience in the professional degree program.
ATHTR 810: This course will focus on the etiology, evaluation and rehabilitation of injuries to the pelvic girdle, spine, thoracic cage and head typically encountered by physically active individuals.
ATHTR 811: This reflects the third clinical education experience in the professional degree program.
ATHTR 812: This elective course offers students a broad array of potential clerkships that foster growth of professional knowledge, skills, attitude, and habits through direct patient/client care experiences, pedagogical, and/or research training opportunities.
ATHTR 813: This course is designed to provide students with professional knowledge of the administrative aspects of delivering athletic training services in healthcare systems.
ATHTR 814: This represents the fourth clinical education experience in the professional degree program.
ATHTR 815: This course is designed to provide students with knowledge that lends to their professional development through interactions with an array of personnel who operate in the broad spectrum of sports health care.
ATHTR 816: This final experiential learning course facilitates the graduating athletic training student's entry into the profession.
ATHTR 817: This course is designed to serve as a mechanism by which students engage in scholarly work through a series of guided, and self-directed knowledge translation activities that involve the integration of skills acquired throughout the academic plan.
ATHTR 897: Formal course given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
